summary: SIEM feed s130_double is degraded: 12.3% of frames exceed the tool's 1518-byte MTU and are dropped at the NIC, and 52.2% of traffic remains ERSPAN-encapsulated and opaque to the SIEM.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is forwarding jumbo/ERSPAN-enlarged frames up to 8108 bytes to a 1 Gbps SIEM port with 1518-byte MTU without slicing or MTU handling. The NIC drops oversized frames on ingress.
findings.impact_on_tool: 396 of 3219 frames (12.3%) are silently dropped before SIEM processing, creating blind spots for detection and correlation. SIEM does not need full payload so loss is avoidable.

recommended_fix.why: SIEM needs_full_payload=false, so broker can slice/trim frames to 1518 bytes to fit the tool port MTU while preserving headers for SIEM analysis, preventing NIC drops.

findings.root_cause: Broker is delivering ERSPAN-encapsulated traffic directly to the SIEM without stripping the tunnel header. 1679 of 3219 frames (52.2%) are still inside ERSPAN.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM cannot parse inner IP/transport headers or apply rules/content inspection to encapsulated traffic; over half of traffic is effectively invisible, severely reducing detection coverage.

recommended_fix.why: Strip ERSPAN encapsulation on the packet broker so the SIEM receives the inner original packets it can parse and correlate.
